milestones.name: A merge's check no longer runs the ten-minute gale, the stepped hour, the field flythroughs or the shore-blend solve, and they pass in release on main after each merge
milestones.quality_bar: As careful as a test-suite reduction in a well-kept engine such as Bevy or wgpu: the merge check gets shorter, every assertion that was made is still made somewhere that runs, and anyone can see where.

items.statement: `./dev check` runs none of the six long tests the design's table names for this milestone: the ten-minute gale on Metal, the exit scene's stepped hour, the three field flythroughs and the shore-blend solve. Each is an ignored test whose reason starts `long:` and names the command that runs it, with the body and every assertion it had. The other tests of those binaries run in `./dev check` as they did.
items.check: sh -c 'test "$(cargo test --locked --offline -p water-scene -p v1-game -p thrum-water-model --tests -- --list --ignored 2>/dev/null | grep -cE "(^|::)(actual_gale_keeps_the_fleet_in_contact_on_metal|movers_keep_their_authored_loops_after_a_stepped_hour|field_culling_matches_direct_along_the_flythrough|mixed_mesh_field_frustum_matches_bucket_direct_along_the_flythrough|mixed_mesh_occlusion_matches_bucket_direct_through_first_cut|both_blends_against_component_own_solve_and_nearest_negative_control): test$")" -eq 6'
items.ask: Compare the six tests with the starting commit: is anything changed but the ignore attribute? Is any other test of those files ignored, shortened or removed?

items.statement: `./dev long-tests` runs every long test and no other ignored test, in a release build with overflow checks on, on the toolchain `./dev check` uses, and a GPU test that finds no adapter fails in it where it would have skipped. Its list names the foam scene's test binary too. `./dev help` lists it, and `ORCHESTRATE.md` declares the main-branch check `long-tests` in the design's words.
items.check: sh -c './dev help | grep -q long-tests && grep -q "Main-branch check long-tests:" ORCHESTRATE.md'
items.ask: Read the command. Does it run each of the six tests of M1.1, and can it run an ignored test that is not a long test, such as the cooked valley route's? Does it set what makes a GPU test fail where no adapter is found, build in release with overflow checks on, and use the toolchain `./dev check` uses? Is the settings line the design's, word for word?

items.statement: The six long tests pass in the main-branch check `long-tests`, on main at the claimed commit.

milestones.name: Nothing in a merge's check is built and run twice, and the atmosphere's Monte Carlo reference no longer runs in it
milestones.quality_bar: As careful as a test-suite reduction in a well-kept engine such as Bevy or wgpu: the merge check gets shorter, every assertion that was made is still made somewhere that runs, and anyone can see where.

items.statement: `thrum-water`'s swash test runs in one test binary, where it ran in two.

`thrum-clouds`' GPU conformance runs once on the native device and once on WebGPU's default limits, where four test binaries made those two runs between them. The two tests that stay keep their names, `coarse_sun_paths_match_the_cpu_reference` and `weather_and_sun_path_work_with_default_limits`, and every assertion the four made is made by one of the two.
items.check: sh -c 'test "$(cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-clouds --tests -- --list 2>/dev/null | grep -cE "(coarse_sun_paths_match_the_cpu_reference|weather_and_sun_path_work_with_default_limits): test$")" -eq 2 && test "$(cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-clouds --tests -- --list 2>/dev/null | grep -cE "(broken_sky_factor_has_no_floor_or_border_switch|columns_and_integer_cells_match_the_cpu_at_their_written_tick): test$")" -eq 0 && THRUM_REQUIRE_GPU=1 cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-clouds'
items.ask: How many times does `cargo test -p thrum-clouds` now run the weather loop and the Sun-path checks: once on the native device and once on default limits? Take the weather-map, Sun-path and continuity assertions of the four old files: is each still made in one of the two runs?

items.statement: The dense field's frustum-only mixed-mesh flythrough is gone, because the occlusion flythrough builds the same direct and frustum hosts and makes the same frustum assertions. The two flythroughs that are left are long tests in one test binary, which `./dev long-tests` runs.
items.check: sh -c '! git grep -q "fn mixed_mesh_field_frustum_matches_bucket_direct_along_the_flythrough" -- crates examples && git grep -q "fn mixed_mesh_occlusion_matches_bucket_direct_through_first_cut" -- examples && git grep -q "fn field_culling_matches_direct_along_the_flythrough" -- examples'
items.ask: Does the occlusion flythrough still run the frustum host and assert on it exactly as the deleted test did? Do the two tests left build into one binary, are both still ignored as long tests, and does the list of `./dev long-tests` name that binary and no binary that is gone?

items.statement: The older copy of the cloud display-phase test is gone, and the display-phase test that `CLOUDS` M2.11 replaced it with is unchanged.

The atmosphere's Monte Carlo reference is not built or run by `./dev check`: the f64 path tracer, the quadrature, the random walks, their 198-case run and the tests of the reference itself are out of the tree. The night checks still run as they did. The twilight guard runs as a test of its own, with the three expected values written in it, its 2.5% bound on each channel and its atlas-plane checks as they were.
items.check: sh -c '! git grep -q "fn adaptive_refinement_and_direct_first_order_monte_carlo_agree" -- crates && git grep -q "fn night_profile_survives_sky_sampling_and_the_incident_reduction" -- crates && THRUM_REQUIRE_GPU=1 cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-render --lib atmosphere::gpu'
items.ask: Is any f64 path tracer, quadrature or random-walk reference still compiled by `./dev check`? Does the night test assert what it asserted at the starting commit? Which test runs the twilight guard now, and are its three expected values, its 2.5% bound and its atlas-plane checks the ones the starting commit held, with nothing recomputed?

milestones.name: A merge's check no longer runs the foam's ten-minute moored run, which passes on main after each merge, and still runs the wind sweep

items.statement: `./dev check` no longer runs the moored foam scenes for ten minutes. That run is a long test of its own, on the sea and on the lake, with every assertion it had, and its reason starts `long:`. The wind sweep is a test of its own that `./dev check` runs: mean foam cover rises across the three winds, as it was asserted.
items.check: sh -c 'cargo test --locked --offline -p water-scene --test foam_scene_gpu -- --list --ignored | grep -q ": test$" && THRUM_REQUIRE_GPU=1 cargo test --locked --offline -p water-scene --test foam_scene_gpu'
items.ask: Compare the two tests with the starting commit's one: does the ignored test make every moored assertion, at every tick it was made, and the wind-sweep test every wind assertion? When the ignored test is run, does its child process run the test and not skip it?

items.statement: The ten-minute moored run passes in the main-branch check `long-tests`, on main at the claimed commit.

items.statement: The cooked cloud march is no longer held to an f64 transport sum. A short test draws through the real cooked contribution, with the cloud-factor shader variant: zero density leaves the sky as it was, density darkens it, and the test fails if the variant's text replacement did not match.

milestones.name: The check builds and runs its tests the fastest way a measurement supports, and the record says how long a merge's check and the long tests take now
milestones.quality_bar: As measured as a build-profile change in a well-kept Rust workspace such as Bevy's or wgpu's: timed both ways on one commit before it is switched on, with the same tests passing after as before.

items.statement: The record times `./dev check` on one commit three ways: as it is; with dependencies optimised in test builds; and with test binaries run by nextest, GPU tests held to two at once. Each way is run twice, alternating, and each run has its wall time, the load average and what else was running.
items.ask: Does the record hold two runs of each of the three arrangements on one commit, alternated and not grouped, each with its load? Is the build time of a changed profile counted in its runs or stated beside them?

items.statement: An arrangement is on in `./dev check` only if both of its runs were shorter than both runs of the check as it was. Where both are on, the run that gives the check's time afterwards is shorter than both of those runs too, or the arrangement that won by less is off. One that did not win is left out, and the record says so. Test builds keep debug assertions and overflow checks. Where nextest is on, a machine without it still runs every test through `cargo test`, doc tests still run, and tests that share a device through an in-process lock run one at a time.
items.ask: Read the record and the diff. Is each arrangement that is on one that won both ways, and if two are on, did the pair beat the check as it was? Do test builds keep debug assertions and overflow checks? If nextest is on: what runs where it is not installed, do doc tests run, and are the files that guard GPU residency or device loss with a mutex held to one test at a time?

items.statement: Every test that ran and passed in `./dev check` before this milestone still runs and passes in it on this Mac, and none is skipped; a test the check ran twice may now run once. The record holds the test results before and after, the later run made with `THRUM_REQUIRE_GPU=1`.
items.ask: Compare the two recorded runs test by test, not their totals: does every test that reported ok before report ok after, at least once? Does the later run hold any `thrum-gpu-skip:` line?

items.statement: `./dev check` runs each cooked-asset test once against the production build, in the workspace pass, and its draw-probe pass runs only the tests that assert on the draw probe.
items.ask: Which tests of the cooked-assets binary read the draw probe? Does the probe pass run each of them and no other test of that binary, and does the workspace pass still run all of them?

items.statement: The record gives a merge's check time at this module's start, 33 to 45 minutes on 20 November, and now, and how long one run of `./dev long-tests` takes, each on this Mac with the load recorded. `CONTRIBUTING.md` says what `./dev check` runs, what `./dev long-tests` runs on main after the merge, and how to run one long test by hand.
items.ask: Do the record's times for the check and for the long tests come from runs at the claimed commit, each with its load? Does `CONTRIBUTING.md` name the two commands and say how to run one long test by hand?
